rows.rationale: Makes the speaker explicit while preserving threatened sexual humiliation.
rows.before: “Look, I am against you,” says the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face; I will show nations your nakedness and kingdoms your shame.
rows.after: “Look, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Armies. “I will lift your skirts over your face and show the nations your nakedness, the kingdoms your disgrace.
rows.tsw_comparator: “Look, I am against you,” says the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face; I will show nations your nakedness and kingdoms your shame.

rows.after: Yet she too was carried away into captivity. Her little children were dashed to pieces at every street corner. Lots were cast for her honored men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
rows.tsw_comparator: Yet she also went into exile, she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her honored ones, and all her great ones were bound in chains.

rows.rationale: Preserves the gendered taunt and gate-bar image; its ancient insult is not converted into a claim about women today.
rows.before: Look, your troops within you are like women. The gates of your land are opened wide to your enemies; fire consumes your bars.
rows.after: Look at your people: women in your midst! Your land’s gates stand wide open to your enemies; fire has eaten through their bars.
rows.tsw_comparator: Look, your troops within you are like women. The gates of your land are opened wide to your enemies; fire consumes your bars.
